tools.name: create_upload_url
tools.description: Preferred way to host a file. Reserves a link and returns a short-lived upload_url on filetourl.org itself, safe for AI agent sandboxes that only allow egress to trusted domains, since the upload never has to leave filetourl.org. Send the raw file bytes yourself with a single HTTP PUT to that URL (d

tools.name: confirm_upload
tools.description: Optional. Confirm that the PUT to a create_upload_url upload_url finished, and get the final size and link back. The link also activates without this call, this just verifies it.

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Host a small file by sending its bytes inline as base64. Prefer create_upload_url instead: inline base64 is slow and costly above roughly 100KB. For a user's own files only. Needs a FileToUrl Developer API key.

tools.name: get_file_status
tools.description: Look up whether a link created earlier is still active. Reports 'pending' for a reserved upload whose bytes have not arrived yet, and 'expired' once its upload window has passed.

tools.name: start_upload
tools.description: Begin a chunked upload for larger files. Returns an upload_id and recommended chunk size. Use this instead of upload_file for files over ~2MB.

tools.name: upload_chunk
tools.description: Send one chunk of a file started with start_upload. Call repeatedly with increasing chunk_index (starting at 0) until the whole file is sent, then call finish_upload.

tools.name: finish_upload
tools.description: Complete a chunked upload after all chunks have been sent via upload_chunk. Assembles the file, uploads it, and returns the shareable URL.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_upload_url · Private data: create_upload_url, upload_file, get_file_status, start_upload, upload_chunk, finish_upload · Public sink: create_upload_url, confirm_upload, upload_file, get_file_status, start_upload, upload_chunk, finish_upload.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_upload_url · Private data: create_upload_url, upload_file, get_file_status, start_upload, upload_chunk, finish_upload · Public sink: create_upload_url, confirm_upload, upload_file, get_file_status, start_upload, upload_chunk, finish_upload

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "upload_file" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Host a file publicly and receive a shareable link back. For a user's own files only. Needs a FileToUrl Developer API key." → after: "Host a small file by sending its bytes inline as base64. Prefer create_upload_url instead: inline base64 is slow and costly above roughly 100KB. For a user's own files only. Needs a FileToUrl Developer API key."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
